deck.caption:
A single phone call cost two people Rs 7.2 lakh. In the world of digital banking, your biggest risk isn't the market—it's the person on the other end of the line. 

• Why 'urgent' bank calls are red flags
• The truth about credit card verification
• How to protect your savings from fake agents

Save this to keep your bank account safe. If a bank representative calls you claiming your card is blocked, do you hang up and call the official number, or do you follow their instructions?

slides.title: One Phone Call. Rs 7.2 Lakh Lost. The Math of Fraud.
slides.body: Two individuals recently lost a combined Rs 7.2 lakh in a single, calculated credit card scam. Here is how it happened and how you can avoid being next.

comparison_data.myth: Banks call you to demand immediate action or fund transfers to 'verify' your credit card.
comparison_data.reality: Legitimate banks never ask for sensitive credentials or money transfers over an unsolicited phone call.

slides.title: How the Scam Works
flowchart_data: 1. You receive a call from someone claiming to be a bank official.
2. They create a sense of panic regarding your credit card status.
3. They direct you to a fake link or ask for your OTP/PIN.
4. Your account is drained before you realize the fraud.

stat_data.label: Total loss reported by two victims
stat_data.context: This amount represents the life savings or hard-earned capital of two individuals targeted by a single scam operation.

checklist_data.item: Pressure to click a link sent via SMS

slides.title: The Golden Rule of Banking
slides.card_text: If you receive a call about your credit card, hang up immediately. Do not provide information. Instead, open your bank's official mobile app or visit your nearest branch to check your account status.

slides.title: Why Uncertainty is Your Shield
slides.card_text: Never assume a caller is who they say they are. Even if they know your name or card details, treat every unsolicited request for sensitive information as a potential threat to your financial security.

slides.title: Protect Your Hard-Earned Money
slides.cta_detail: Takeaway: Never share OTPs or click links from unknown callers. Always verify by calling the official bank number found on the back of your card. Save this post to remind your family.
